title: Complete 6-Month SQL & Data Engineering Roadmap (100% Free)
post_text:
SQL is tested in 100% of Data Science and Data Engineering interviews.

Here is the exact zero-cost roadmap to master SQL from scratch to advanced window functions:

Month 1: Fundamentals & Relational Algebra
- SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, HAVING
- Aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX)
- Practice: SQLZoo & Mode Analytics SQL Tutorial

Month 2: Joins & Set Operations
- INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER JOINs
- UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT
- Self-joins and Cross-joins in real production queries

Month 3: Advanced SQL & Analytical Functions
- Window Functions: ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), NTILE()
- Value Functions: LAG(), LEAD(), FIRST_VALUE(), LAST_VALUE()
- Common Table Expressions (WITH clauses) & Recursive CTEs

Month 4: Query Optimization & Indexing
- B-Tree vs Hash Indexing
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE execution plan breakdown
- Eliminating correlated subqueries and table scans

title: Free Deep Learning & Computer Vision Foundations from Stanford
post_text:
How Convolutional Neural Networks actually process image tensors:

1. Convolution Layer:
Applies kernel filters across the spatial input volume to extract local feature maps (edges, textures, shapes).

2. Activation (ReLU / GELU):
Introduces non-linearity, allowing the network to compute complex boundary mappings without vanishing gradients.

3. Pooling (Max / Average):
Reduces spatial resolution while preserving dominant feature activations, providing translational invariance.

4. Fully Connected Layers & Softmax:
Flattens high-dimensional feature activations into class probability distributions.

Attached is the official Stanford CS230 CNN and Deep Learning Architecture cheatsheet.

title: Distributed Data Processing with Dask & Python
post_text:
When your Pandas dataframe exceeds RAM, you don't need to immediately rewrite everything in PySpark.

Dask lets you scale native Python code across multiple CPU cores and distributed clusters:

1. Dask DataFrame:
Parallelizes Pandas operations across chunked partitions, executing out-of-core calculations seamlessly.

2. Dask Array:
Extends NumPy ndarrays across distributed memory blocks for massive matrix algebra.

3. Dynamic Task Graphs:
Dask builds lazy computational DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs) and optimizes execution before running tasks.

Attached is the complete Dask Distributed computing cheatsheet by Favio Vázquez.

title: PySpark DataFrame & Big Data Architecture Guide
post_text:
PySpark architecture and big data engineering reference:

1. Catalyst Optimizer:
Converts declarative Spark SQL and DataFrame queries into optimized physical execution plans.

2. Tungsten Execution Engine:
Manages off-heap memory allocation and generates whole-stage code generation for hardware-level CPU cache efficiency.

3. Partitioning & Shuffling:
Avoid wide dependencies (groupBy, join without broadcast) across worker nodes to eliminate network bottlenecks.

title: Transformer Architecture & Self-Attention Mathematical Breakdown
post_text:
The landmark 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' replaced recurrent networks with pure Multi-Head Attention mechanisms.

Core Building Blocks:
1. Scaled Dot-Product Attention:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V

2. Multi-Head Projection:
Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

3. Positional Encodings:
Since there is no recurrence or convolution, sinusoidal positional encodings inject relative token order.

Attached is the original landmark research paper from Google Brain.

title: Stanford CS229: Mathematics & Linear Algebra for Machine Learning
post_text:
Before you train complex neural networks, mastering fundamental linear algebra and multivariable calculus is essential.

Key Mathematical Pillars:

2. Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) & Spectral Decomposition
3. Vector Calculus: Gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, and Taylor Series Expansions
4. Matrix Derivatives: Deriving loss functions with respect to weight matrices

title: Fine-Tuning LLMs with LoRA & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
post_text:
Full parameter fine-tuning of 70B+ LLMs requires massive GPU clusters. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices.

Why LoRA is Revolutionary:
1. Reduces trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory footprint by 3x.
2. Injects low-rank decomposition matrices W0 + B*A into Transformer attention layers.
3. Zero inference latency overhead: trained adapter weights can be merged directly into base weights during deployment.

Attached is the original LoRA research paper by Edward Hu et al. from Microsoft.
